question: Is the named UK entity active?
finding: Companies House labels Gigaton Technologies Ltd, no. 12942593, Active and shows the former Carbon Re Ltd name through 26 May 2026.
evidence_note: Public record
confidence: High for register status on access date; supported
limits: Shows registration status only; says nothing about financial position or any other entity.
next_test: Recheck before Stage 7/10.

question: Was there a recent leading-VC round?
finding: UCL Ventures announced a $26m Series A led by Plural on 3 Jun 2026, with 2150 and others.
evidence_note: Company/investor-reported
confidence: Medium for announced transaction; partly supported pending financing documents
limits: Closing date, subscribed amount, issuer, price, allocation and rights not established here.
next_test: Seek independent/registry corroboration and terms if material.

question: Is there a concrete cement deployment example?
finding: Gigaton's Mokra case reports a 2.2% reduction in specific heat consumption and says its AI enhanced ABB Expert Optimizer.
evidence_note: Company-reported, with quote attributed to plant director
confidence: Medium for existence of named case; low-to-medium for quantified effect and contract economics
limits: Full results behind contact form; baseline, measurement and paid status unavailable.
next_test: Seek customer-side confirmation and full methodology if accessible.

question: What customer/economic claims accompanied the round?
finding: UCL Ventures names Adani, Heidelberg and Holcim and reports $1m–$3m savings/up to 30,000 tCO₂ per plant; 2150 gives c.£1.3m/6,000 tCO₂ for a plant.
evidence_note: Investor-associated claims; two investor sources give different figures, and neither is independent.
confidence: Medium for published claims; low for representative realised economics
limits: Different measures may refer to different plants/scopes; not independent verification or supplier revenue.
next_test: Request site-level before/after and contract evidence at diligence; test sensitivity at Stage 3.

question: Is advanced cement process control already served?
finding: ABB sells cement APC for kiln, alternative fuels and related units and describes AI/ML features; FLSmidth markets ECS/ProcessExpert.
source_title: ABB Ability Expert Optimizer | FLSmidth Cement ECS/ProcessExpert brochure
evidence_note: Supplier primary descriptions; counter-evidence: incumbent suppliers already sell advanced kiln process control.
confidence: High for available product categories; low for independent comparative performance
limits: Supplier installations/ROI claims not externally validated here.
next_test: Compare workflows, control rights, incremental results and procurement.

question: Does the current product still appear ABB-only?
finding: Gigaton's current product page describes autonomous control connecting directly to the DCS and an augmentation case at Mokra.
evidence_note: Company-reported
confidence: Medium for present positioning; Low for commercial eligibility across stacks
limits: Website scope is broader than verified contracts/configurations.
next_test: Test configurations and product/control permissions by paid deployment.

question: Does the Mokra case describe how incremental gain was measured?
finding: Cambridge Enterprise describes a month-on/month-off evaluation controlling for fuel mix/raw material quality and reports 2.2% lower specific heat consumption.
evidence_note: Investor-associated account citing company/customer evaluation
confidence: Medium for described methodology; Low-to-Medium for causal effect/transferability
limits: Raw data, longer-term performance, contract economics and independent replication unavailable. Not separate independent validation of E-007.
next_test: Seek original evaluation, seasonality/counterfactual and persistent net benefits.

question: Can summary counts be traced to assets and metadata?
finding: The July 2026 plant data has 3,884 unique plant IDs; metadata defines physical existing kiln stock irrespective of operating status and numeric-count accuracy. No APC/DCS/data-readiness fields.
source_title: Global Energy Monitor, Global Cement and Concrete Tracker, July 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0 (licence: https://globalenergymonitor.org/creative-commons-license); counts calculated from the downloadable dataset
evidence_note: Third-party research estimate
confidence: High for schema and extracted records; Medium for complete current coverage
limits: Source status is plant-level; cement output is CY2024/FY2025 and is not clinker output.
next_test: E-046 preserves filters and missingness; active-line and priced-unit evidence still needed.

question: What did recovered data actually narrow?
finding: The gap calculations reproduce 2,521 sites, 1,359 with ≥1 Mtpa reported capacity, 1,338 also dry, 431 also AF yes; 678 capacity unknowns. 3,697 physical kilns at operating sites are not active lines.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation using E-039
confidence: High for tested arithmetic; Low as SAM/pricing evidence
limits: Illustrative threshold, missing capacity, no compatibility/ready-site census. 431 is not a lower-bound SAM.
next_test: Price and readiness remain open; use physical segment for later research only.

question: Is there an adjacent annual fee reference?
finding: Braincube "Basic" directory listing is USD 7,000.00/month (re-checked 13 Nov 2026), annualised to USD 84k. No unit or scope established.
evidence_note: Third-party listing and analyst calculation; the earlier fee proxy, kept as history (replaced as the main comparison by E-108).
confidence: Low for applicability
limits: Different product; unit and scope not established. Not verified vendor pricing or cement contract evidence.
next_test: Obtain actual quote/unit or additional matched pricing.

question: Does Braincube itself establish the fee?
finding: Prices are set in each statement of work; published terms do not validate the directory figure.
source_title: Braincube general terms and conditions, Article 11
evidence_note: Braincube's own terms and conditions; counter-evidence to the listed fee in E-047.
confidence: Medium for historical commercial structure
limits: No numeric tariff.
next_test: Current commercial evidence if material.

question: Provisional TAM/SAM and sanity check
finding: Site-wide assumed USD 84k/year yields USD 211.764m TAM; SAM uses ≥1 Mtpa capacity, 50% of 678 unknown-capacity sites and 70% conditional readiness, yielding USD 99.8424m. Against a wider APC market estimate, implied ratios 6.9%/3.2%.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation and inference
confidence: High arithmetic confidence, Low market-estimate confidence.
limits: Fee transfer, unit, size, unknown-capacity and readiness are explicit assumptions, not measured facts. Potential revenue compared with broader actual-spend estimates.
next_test: User review, later price/unit and economic/readiness validation; not SOM or Stage 4 approval.

question: Does older augmentation evidence validate the current product?
finding: Management describes evolution beyond earlier layering towards control of both control/optimisation layers, with a customer-maintained-control exception.
evidence_note: Company-reported, with analyst inference
confidence: Medium for stated strategy, Low actual version/deployment mix.
limits: Neither new-product success nor incumbent failure independently established.
next_test: Map product generation, control authority, customer result and contract scope.

question: Is there partner-side delivery detail?
finding: Rajiv Engineers describes Gigaton partnership and consultation, integration, commissioning, training and ongoing support.
source_title: Rajiv Engineers partnership | Rajiv Engineers AI cement automation
evidence_note: Partner-reported
confidence: Medium for advertised responsibilities; Medium route specificity; Low realised capacity/economics.
limits: Generic welding testimonial is not AI proof; no share/exclusivity/rights disclosed.
next_test: Agreement, staffing, delivery effort, support allocation and retained revenue.

question: What can public diligence and scenarios establish?
finding: First bounded assessment retains five priorities/eight workstreams. The first scenario model covers new-cohort opportunity and synthetic INR value with explicit assumptions, not actual willingness, ARR or validated SOM.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation/inference; builds on E-021, E-047 and E-052
confidence: High tested arithmetic reliability; Low applicability/investment-case confidence.
limits: Actual paid base Unknown, whole-company output Not estimated. Scenario assumptions are not observed source actuals.
next_test: Review Stage 9 and decide whether to authorise qualified Stage 10 synthesis or pause for decisive access.

question: Matched retention anchor?
finding: Published USD 50k–100k ACV GRR quartiles: 80% at the 25th percentile, 90% at the median and 95% at the 75th percentile; overall GRR sample 225.
evidence_note: Primary benchmark-publisher survey
confidence: High reported-value reliability; High source reading; Low company applicability. Supported narrowly.
limits: Revenue retention, not logo/site renewal; industrial subset unavailable.
next_test: Apply as fee-equivalent revenue proxy, test sensitivities and replace with actual cohorts if available.

question: Proposal conversion anchor?
finding: Half of respondents report 31–50% win rates after proposal.
source_title: Norwest 2024 Sales and Marketing Benchmark Report, pp. 3, 52, 53
evidence_note: Primary survey-publisher account
confidence: High reported-value reliability; High source reading, Low industrial transferability.
limits: 40% selected near band centre, not surveyed median; 25% downside stress. 9/12 month cycle selected by analyst, not quoted statistic.
next_test: Match funnel stage; keep within-year deployment acceptance separate and Low confidence.

question: Adjacent channel-share anchor?
finding: Programme publishes 20% monthly recurring net-revenue share up to 3 years, subject to eligibility.
evidence_note: HubSpot's own programme policy
confidence: High for own stated terms; High policy reading, Low industrial transferability.
limits: Does not price Rajiv Engineers' engineering or establish its contract.
next_test: Revised 70% capture = 1 − 20% proxy − 10 percentage-point analyst service allocation; validate actual sharing/costs later.

question: Educated model revision and implication?
finding: Revised source screen 183 sites, 137 known large/15 unknown/31 below; proposal pools 6/24/36 derive from workload. Reference incremental annual opportunity USD 582,758.40 at 2 Nov 2029.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation/inference
confidence: High tested arithmetic/source extraction reliability; Low applicability.
limits: Candidate fit/access not established; staffing/cycles/acceptance reasoned, not observed. Existing paid base remains Unknown; full-company output Not estimated. Original E-081 superseded for current scenario use.
next_test: Actual contracts, capacity, financials and terms remain decisive. No automatic Stage 10 approval.

question: Reported deployment scale?
finding: A Gigaton job advert describes 9 plants live and a goal of 50 by 31 December 2027. Paid state and industry mix not disclosed.
evidence_note: Company-reported target in a job advert.
confidence: Medium for the reported starting count; Low as independent commercial evidence.
limits: The posting date does not prove the text is unchanged. "Live" is not the same as paying, and nine is not the paid starting base.
next_test: Reconcile the plant list, product version, acceptance, contracts and payments.

question: Does counting kilns instead of sites change the count?
finding: The 2,521 operating sites have 3,697 physical kilns, about 47% more than the site count. Physical kilns include inactive units and are not active or billable units.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation using the E-039 dataset.
confidence: Medium for physical stock; Low for commercial meaning.
limits: Inactive, approximate and minimum counts are included. A fee per kiln would be hypothetical, not a quote.
next_test: An active-kiln census, the charging unit, bundling or discounts, and the savings base.

question: Is the move beyond cement entirely unevidenced?
finding: UKRI Gateway to Research records a closed project led by Carbon Re Ltd (Gigaton's former name): a feasibility study of an AI platform to improve energy efficiency in steel and glass manufacture, funded value GBP 202,022, 1 March 2022 to 31 August 2023. Gigaton's glass page (company-reported) describes feasibility work and its steel page invites pilot projects.
source_title: UKRI Gateway to Research, project 10015490 | Gigaton glass page | Gigaton steel page
evidence_note: Public record for the grant; the glass and steel pages are company-reported.
confidence: High for the historical award; Low for current commercial readiness.
limits: A closed grant is not assumed to be active. No outcome report was reviewed. Research and pilot material is not commercial evidence.
next_test: Current product, performance in each sector, paid acceptance, charging unit and price, before any sizing.

question: A better documented supplier fee comparison?
finding: Braincube Real Time Process Optimization is listed at USD 67,530.48 a year (one-year subscription): "The standard package covers up to 10 optimization units across up to 2 sites." A notice gives USD 155,000.00 a year from 3/1/2027 (UTC), read as 1 March 2027.
source_title: Braincube Real Time Process Optimization, Microsoft Marketplace listing and price notice
evidence_note: Braincube's own listing; a vendor offer, not a transaction.
confidence: High for the wording, price and date shown on access; Low for transfer to Gigaton.
limits: A different product that recommends settings. "Optimisation unit" is not defined; units per plant, implementation and support are unknown. List prices are not contract prices (E-048).
next_test: A matched scope or current contract. Count two-site use only where a customer actually shares the package.

question: How do package use and price date change the market?
finding: At 2,521 operating sites and 1,188.6 serviceable site-equivalents, SAM is USD 40.13m (current price, 2 sites), 80.27m (current price, 1 site), 92.12m (from 1 March 2027, 2 sites) and 184.23m (from 1 March 2027, 1 site). The announced price is 2.295 times the current one.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation using E-046 and E-108.
confidence: High for tested arithmetic; Low for market applicability.
limits: Four separate dated cases, not a fee range. Filters held fixed, though higher prices may reduce eligibility. The ten-unit limit and site pairings are not validated. One vendor does not show a category trend.
next_test: Validate the unit, eligibility at each price and scope in the exit year.

question: Fundraising dilution benchmark?
finding: Carta chart of 1,133 US software rounds in the six months to 10 July 2026. Dilution at the 25th percentile / median / 75th percentile: Series A 11/18/21%; B 8.6/12/16.4%; C 5.6/9.8/15%; D 3.9/8.1/11.8%.
source_title: Carta data, LinkedIn archive (chart posted 10 July 2026)
evidence_note: Carta's own round data; adjacent US software, not matched to Gigaton.
confidence: High for the chart values; Low for application to Gigaton.
limits: Separate statistics for each stage, not ownership tracked over time. Whole-round dilution is not one investor's stake. The actual round structure is unknown.
next_test: Actual round terms, option pool, instruments and later funding path; evidence matched on geography and industry.

question: What supports the sale multiple?
finding: SEG's 2Q26 report, page 10: the median sale value of SaaS companies acquired, as a multiple of revenue over the past twelve months (EV/TTM revenue), fell from 4.2x to 4.0x; the average fell from 6.3x to 6.2x.
source_title: Software Equity Group, 2Q26 SaaS M&A and Public Market Report, p. 10 (copy hosted by SandHill)
evidence_note: SEG-authored report in a copy hosted by a third party.
confidence: High for the reported values; Low for transfer to Gigaton.
limits: 4x has an adjacent benchmark; 10x is an analyst sensitivity, not a SEG endpoint. Transactions not recalculated; TTM revenue is not ARR.
next_test: Better matched transactions, with growth, margin and exit context.

question: Why test 3x and 10x returns, and how old is the source?
finding: A historical practitioner article links 10x-plus returns on early-stage winners, and 3x on later-stage winners, to different holding periods and risk.
source_title: Industry Ventures, The Venture Capital Risk and Return Matrix
evidence_note: Industry Ventures' own practitioner view; context, not a benchmark.
confidence: High for page content and dates; Low as any investor's actual target.
limits: Page shows 2.7.17; metadata gives 8 February 2017, modified 12 October 2021; the cited fund series ends 31 December 2014. A modification date does not show the analysis was refreshed. A gross multiple is not an internal rate of return.
next_test: The actual investor's objective, holding period, preferences and follow-on cash flows.

question: Is there a premium industrial-software precedent?
finding: Emerson's announcement gives AspenTech a whole-company enterprise value of USD 16.8bn; AspenTech's FY2024 results (year to 30 June 2024) give revenue of USD 1,127.482m. Dividing gives 14.90x, tested separately as a rounded 15x case.
source_title: Emerson announcement | AspenTech FY2024 results (SEC filing)
evidence_note: Emerson's and AspenTech's own disclosures, with analyst calculation.
confidence: High for the arithmetic; Low for direct comparability.
limits: A controlling shareholder buying out the minority of a mature, broad platform; the whole-company value differs from the USD 7.2bn stake purchase. Not a company-quoted or TTM multiple.
next_test: Match period, business scope and control context before using it.

question: Does the gap hold across all tested cases?
finding: At an 18% stake and 72.946544% kept after rounds B to D, a 10x return on USD 26m needs USD 198.01m to 495.04m of annual revenue at 10 to 4 times revenue. The favourable constructed case needs USD 149.32m at 10 times, 81.05% of the USD 184.233m SAM; the B and C path needs USD 181.97m, 98.77%.
evidence_note: Analyst calculation using E-002, E-108 and E-110 to E-113.
confidence: High for tested arithmetic; Low for applicability to the company.
limits: Illustrative: the inputs are benchmarks and assumptions, not the investors' terms or targets. Constructed cases are not ownership percentiles. The 20–30% share has no benchmark. It does not rule out every tested case.
next_test: Validate fees and unit, attainable share, the market's time horizon, actual terms and the company's scope.
